subject: Post-call recap & prompt set request - ACME model fit
messages:
From: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Bob Lee <bob@acme.com>, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Today's discovery call (model fit + next steps)

Thanks for the call today - useful conversation. A couple quick clarifications from our side:

- We primarily need reliable generation for customer support summarization and multi-turn chat assistance (average convo length ~8 turns, 512 token context).
- Latency target is p95 < 600ms for 1-2 concurrent requests under steady load; bursts up to 10 req/s are expected during peak.
- Security: we need guidance on PII redaction and how Redwood handles KV cache and logs.

I attached a small sample of real prompts/edge cases (sanitized) - ACME_prompt_examples.csv. Can you confirm the best model candidates and any specific evals we should run? Also will share a procurement timeline once we have a scoped recommendation.

Thanks,
Alice
Alice Nguyen
ML Lead, ACME Corp
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@acme.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Today's discovery call (model fit + next steps)

Hi Alice - great talking with you and Bob earlier. Quick recap + proposed next steps below. I'm looping in Rishi (solutions) and Dev (sales/contract) to help scope an eval and procurement cadence.

Recap:
- Primary workloads: multi-turn chat + concise summarization for support tickets.
- Constraints: p95 latency target ~600ms, sensitive to PII/cross-tenant leakage, prefer hosted initially with an option to move to Dedicated if traffic grows.

Initial recommended models (based on similar deployments):
- redwood-2-small (fastest, good latency for p95 but lower instruction-following on edge cases)
- redwood-2-medium-qa (balanced latency/quality; recommended starting point for chat + summarization)
- redwood-llama-compat-8b-quant (cost-efficient for batch summarization workloads)

Suggested evals and benchmarks:
- Run the ACME prompt set through: redwood-2-small, redwood-2-medium-qa, redwood-llama-compat-8b-quant
- Benchmarks: throughput/latency (p50/p95), summary ROUGE/ROUGE-L and task-specific hallucination checks we can run with your labels
- Regression check: define 20 golden prompts across edge cases and measure semantic similarity + hallucination rate - we can automate alerts on quality regression.

Action items / next steps:
1) Alice: share sanitized prompt set (you attached a draft; thank you) + any golden labels you have for summaries.
2) Rishi & Marissa: we'll stand up a scoped eval and share benchmark links + a preliminary model recommendation by EOD Friday.
3) Dev: will queue procurement template and include estimated committed spend ranges for Dedicated if you'd like that option.

On redaction: Naomi has a short doc with best practices (attached as redaction_guidance.pdf) - I'll flag items that map to our hosted logging/kv-cache retention defaults.

Would you be available for a 30-min check-in Friday morning to review the benchmark results?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 26 Mar 2026 08:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Follow-up: Today's discovery call (model fit + next steps)

Hi Alice - thanks for sending the prompt examples. I pulled out a quick baseline run (small sample) against redwood-2-medium-qa and redwood-llama-compat-8b-quant. Early notes:

- redwood-2-medium-qa: much stronger on instruction following and summarization quality; p95 latency locally ~420ms on a standard hosted config for the sample prompts.
- 8b-quant: cost benefit for batch summarization but tends to truncate longer threads; hallucination rate slightly higher on the edge-case prompts.

I'm attaching the benchmark link with detailed per-prompt metrics: https://redwood.example.com/benchmarks/llm-latency-acme (temporary share).

On PII/redaction: Naomi, can you confirm the hosted defaults we recommend for anonymization hooks and what we advise customers to do pre-ingest vs. at the model layer?

Plan: Marissa/Rishi will run a full eval (200 prompts, golden labels where available) and share the results Friday. If ACME wants to push for p95 < 400ms we can discuss a Dedicated sizing plan.

Thanks,
Rishi
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@acme.com>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 26 Mar 2026 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Follow-up: Today's discovery call (model fit + next steps)

Hi Alice - quick note on redaction guidance and logging:

- Pre-ingest: we recommend removing direct identifiers (SSNs, credit card numbers) at the ingestion pipeline when possible. Use the attached redaction_guidance.pdf for regex templates and PII categories.
- Model layer: for entities that must be retained for context (e.g., ticket numbers), use deterministic token masking and store only hashed references in logs. Avoid storing raw KV cache snapshots in customer-visible logs.
- Hosted defaults: request logs are retained for 30 days; aggregated telemetry (latency, token usage) is retained per your contract. Private/Dedicated customers can configure stricter retention via KMS/HSM integrations.

If ACME can share the golden labels we'll include hallucination classification in the eval and provide per-prompt flags for redaction sensitivity.

Cheers,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Security & Compliance Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@acme.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 26 Mar 2026 09:42:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Follow-up: Today's discovery call (model fit + next steps)

Alice - thanks for the quick turnaround on the sample prompts. I attached a procurement checklist and a draft SOW link in case you want to move forward on Dedicated sizing after the eval.

A couple notes on timelines:
- Eval (scoped run + report): target Fri EOD (2026-03-27)
- Procurement/PO: typical 2-3 week cycle for self-service SaaS; Dedicated reserved capacity lead time ~4-6 weeks after contract sign.

I'm happy to join the Friday check-in if helpful. Proposed time: Fri 10:00-10:30 PT.

Best,
Dev Patel
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
